types.embedding_query_text: Event: A gathering or occurrence with a specific purpose or theme, often involving multiple participants or activities. Also called Celebration, Commemoration, Anniversary, CulturalEvent, PoliticalEvent. Examples: Bayreuth Festival, Silenced Voices, 150th anniversary, Festspielhaus.

chosen_type.label: Event
chosen_type.justification: The general 'Event' class matches all mentions as they are specific instances of gatherings or occurrences.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

candidates.label: Festival
candidates.comment: A Festival is an Event that is a public celebration or series of special events. Also called celebration, gala, fete. Examples: A music festival, a film festival, a cultural heritage festival, a food and wine festival.

candidates.label: SocialEvent
candidates.comment: An event primarily focused on social interaction and entertainment. Also called party, gathering, social function, get-together. Examples: a birthday party, a wedding reception, a community picnic, a networking mixer.

candidates.label: ComedyEvent
candidates.comment: An event featuring comedic performances or content. Also called stand-up show, humor performance, comedy festival. Examples: A stand-up comedy show, a sketch comedy performance, a comedy festival, an improv night. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being, typically identified by name and associated with specific roles or affiliations. Also called Individual, Figure, Artist, Politician, HistoricalFigure. Examples: Michel Friedman, Katharina Wagner, Richard Wagner, Friedrich Merz.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: All mentions are named individuals, aligning with the 'Person' class definition of an individual human being.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

types.embedding_query_text: Opera: A dramatic musical composition performed by singers and musicians, typically involving elaborate staging. Also called MusicalWork, TheatricalProduction, ClassicalOpera, StagePerformance, ArtisticComposition. Examples: Rienzi.

chosen_type.label: MusicComposition
chosen_type.justification: An opera is a musical work, and 'MusicComposition' represents such abstract works, even if they are performed.

candidates.label: MusicComposition
candidates.comment: A MusicComposition is a musical work, such as a song or symphony, that can be performed or recorded. Also called musical piece, song, score. Examples: Beethoven's 5th Symphony, 'Bohemian Rhapsody' by Queen, a jingle. Distinct from MusicRecording, which is a recorded performance of a composition.

candidates.label: Play
candidates.comment: A Play is a CreativeWork in the form of literature, primarily consisting of dialogue between characters, intended for theatrical performance. Also called stage play, drama, theatrical work. Examples: "Hamlet", "Death of a Salesman", "Hamilton", "A Streetcar Named Desire". Distinct from TheaterEvent, which is the actual performance of a play.

candidates.label: PerformingArtsEvent
candidates.comment: A PerformingArtsEvent is an event featuring live performances of arts like music, theatre, dance, or acrobatics. Also called live performance, show, stage event. Examples: a Broadway play, a ballet performance, a circus show, a stand-up comedy act. Distinct from MusicEvent, which is specifically for music.

candidates.label: MusicEvent
candidates.comment: A MusicEvent is an event primarily featuring musical performances. Also called concert, musical performance, gig. Examples: a rock concert, a classical symphony performance, a music festival. Distinct from PerformingArtsEvent, which includes broader performance types like theatre or dance.

candidates.label: MusicRecording
candidates.comment: A MusicRecording, as a CreativeWork, is a recorded performance of a musical composition, usually a single song. Also called music track, song recording, audio track. Examples: 'Yesterday' by The Beatles (the recorded version), a single from an album, a demo track. Distinct from MusicComposition, which is the abstract musical work.

types.embedding_query_text: SocialIssue: A problem affecting a society or community, often related to systemic challenges like discrimination or inequality. Also called SocietalChallenge, PublicProblem, CulturalConflict, EthicalIssue, PoliticalIssue. Examples: Antisemitism.

chosen_type.label: SocialIssue
chosen_type.definition: A societal problem or concern affecting people's lives or communities.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents social issues like antisemitism; 'SocialIssue' is a necessary new type.

candidates.label: PublicationIssue
candidates.comment: A PublicationIssue is a CreativeWork representing a part of a successively published periodical or publication volume, often numbered and containing a grouping of works. Also called journal issue, magazine issue, periodical issue. Examples: "Nature" Vol. 500, Issue 1; "The New Yorker" October 26, 2023 issue; a specific issue of a scientific journal. Distinct from PublicationVolume, which is a larger grouping of issues.

candidates.label: SocialEvent
candidates.comment: An event primarily focused on social interaction and entertainment. Also called party, gathering, social function, get-together. Examples: a birthday party, a wedding reception, a community picnic, a networking mixer.

candidates.label: ComicIssue
candidates.comment: An individual, serially published installment of a comic series, uniquely identified by its series name, volume, issue number, and variant description. Also called comic book, comic installment, single issue comic. Examples: The Amazing Spider-Man #1, Detective Comics Vol. 2 #27, Saga #50, a one-shot comic. Distinct from ComicSeries, which is the overarching publication title.

candidates.label: ActionAccessSpecification
candidates.comment: An ActionAccessSpecification is an Intangible item detailing the requirements that must be met to perform a specific Action. Also called access requirements, action prerequisites, permission rules. Examples: "Requires login," "Subscription needed," "Age 18+," "Admin privileges."

candidates.label: SpecialAnnouncement
candidates.comment: A date-stamped textual information update from a locally-oriented organization, often related to urgent crisis situations, including contextual web links and structured data. Also called public notice, crisis update, community alert, emergency announcement. Examples: a school closure announcement due to weather, a pharmacy's updated operating hours during a pandemic, a local government's public health advisory.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.definition: A calendar date without time component, representing a temporal marker for events.
chosen_type.justification: The mentions are specific calendar dates, fitting the schema.org 'Date' datatype exactly.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: ShippingDeliveryTime
candidates.comment: A structured value providing details about the expected delivery times for product shipping. Also called delivery timeframe, estimated delivery, shipping lead time, transit time. Examples: 'ships in 1-2 business days', 'delivery by Friday', 'estimated 3-5 day transit'.

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

chosen_type.label: Role
chosen_type.justification: The mention describes a person's function in a context, aligning with the schema.org 'Role' class.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: Synagogue
candidates.comment: A civic structure serving as a Jewish house of worship and often a center for community activities. Also called Jewish temple, shul, house of prayer. Examples: 'The Great Synagogue of Rome', a local community synagogue.

candidates.label: DENonprofitType
candidates.comment: DENonprofitType is an enumeration representing specific types of non-profit organizations recognized under German fiscal code, article 52. Also called German non-profit classification, AO 52 non-profit. Examples: A German charitable foundation, a registered German association for public benefit.

candidates.label: PerformanceRole
candidates.comment: A PerformanceRole, as a Role, is a role an entity plays in a theatrical performance, such as a movie or TV series. Also called acting role, character role, stage role. Examples: 'actor in a film', 'director of a play', 'musician in a concert'. Distinct from OrganizationRole, which is a role within an organization.

candidates.label: LiteraryEvent
candidates.comment: An event focused on literature, such as readings, book launches, or discussions. Also called book event, author appearance, literary gathering. Examples: a poetry reading, a book signing, a literary festival, a panel discussion with authors.
